assessment: Quantitative integrity passes. Selective editorial and runtime-pool improvements are recommended; the 4-match/70-percent gate alone does not establish enjoyable or consistent player difficulty.

scope.actualGameModel: Every target has four alternatives. Only one is shown, chosen by hashing the round ID, and stays fixed throughout that round. Easy/Medium/Hard use cumulative 45/110/195 country pools. Assessment never intersects all four alternatives as though the player saw them together.
scope.quantitativeMethod: Independently implemented all 14 name predicates and all 10 population/area predicates against data.js. Numeric intervals were read from their displayed bin IDs, not from stored matches/counts/range objects. Recounted every geography clue by intersecting deduplicated verified matches and declared possible-extra unions with each cumulative pool. Compared computed counts, eligibility, country assignments and texts with runtime exports and openingHintsFor.
scope.geographyBoundary: Geography counts are verified catalog membership counts and declared possibility unions, not an independently proven exhaustive classification of the world. Neither lack of possibleExtraMatches nor a narrow verified list proves complete geographic truth membership. Formal checks are audits of the current catalog and its stated bounds.
scope.playerDifficultyMethod: Qualitative review considers familiar-country recognition, geographic scope conventions, six available guesses, indirect border/area knowledge, distribution of selectable phrases, replay predictability, and redundancy between alternative experiences. Candidate count is evidence of reveal strength, not proof of player knowledge or fun.
scope.frequencyAssumption: Expected frequencies assume approximately uniform targets and approximately uniform hashing among the four positions. Actual journeys exclude prior targets, so per-session rates vary slightly; reported summary rates use the full cumulative pools.
scope.independence: No previous accuracy-review.json, fairness-review.json, or other review verdict was read. The bank status/reviews labels were not used as evidence. No application, generated export or bank changes were made.
scope.externalFactualClaims: No new external geography/population facts are asserted. Country examples and proposed substitutions refer to current embedded data and catalog memberships; future new assignments still require ordinary source verification.

sampleHashSelection.note: A small runtime smoke check supports the approximately uniform four-position assumption; it is not a statistical proof.

historyExclusionReproduction.note: After Hard, startNextRound creates the new Easy puzzle with all three preceding answers excluded, then clears the journey history. Tier-only hint eligibility does not apply those exclusions.

findings.problem: The minimum of four admits shortlists no longer than the six guesses. Easy has 23/180 playable slots with at most six catalog-known candidates (19 have no recorded extras); Medium has 6/440 and Hard 1/780. Familiar groups make some openings substantially more revealing than a broad spelling or population alternative. For Netherlands on Hard, the four known candidate counts are 80,64,7,9; for Algeria they are 86,64,22,6. These small openings are rare across all Hard rounds, so this is a selective consistency concern rather than evidence the whole bank is easy.
findings.playerImplication: If a player knows the full applicable shortlist and convention, they can enumerate a shortlist of at most six within the guess limit without needing the comparative clues. Partial verified geography lists do not justify such a guarantee by themselves.
findings.proposedRemedy: Add a review warning for catalog-known groups of six or fewer on any tier, and a softer warning for familiar-country groups of ten or fewer on Hard. Keep intentionally generous Easy clues where desired. Reassess the inherited Medium/Hard cases individually; for example, give Netherlands one broader currently sourced geography alternative such as Europe or Atlantic coast, and consider Africa in place of North Africa for Algeria on Hard. Do not impose a blanket new minimum merely from these counts.
findings.confidence: high for computed exposure; moderate for player difficulty without playtesting

findings.problem: Tier-only hint eligibility ignores previously excluded answers. A reproduced Greece→Italy→Portugal journey followed by Easy Spain retains the four-member Southern Europe hint although the other three members are unavailable. A player remembering the preceding answers can infer the remaining target.
findings.proposedRemedy: If the minimum of four is intended to guarantee runtime ambiguity, evaluate eligible hint breadth against the actual available target set including history exclusions when the round is created, and save the resulting chosen hint. At minimum, flag small complete groups after exclusions. Preserve the deliberate no-repeat behavior unless the product chooses a different rule.
findings.confidence: high; reproduced through game-state public APIs

findings.problem: Truth-set breadth and display support differ. Six phrases on Easy, four on Medium and six on Hard each have only one display-capable target. In Asia always displays for India, In Africa for Morocco, and In North Africa for Algeria in their applicable pools. This is not a first-time factual giveaway; repeated play can turn a broad clue into a country signature.
findings.proposedRemedy: Track assigned/display-capable target support alongside truth-set counts. Flag singleton display support for editorial review. Where a broad reusable phrase fits several sourced targets, spread it across additional matching countries, or choose a less signature-like existing alternative. Review selection as a bank rather than optimizing each country in isolation.
findings.confidence: high for assignment support; moderate for how quickly players learn it

findings.problem: Easy uses only five name phrases and assigns six-letters-or-fewer to 19/45 countries. Hard uses only 8/14 name phrases: first-letter-after-M appears for 63 countries and consonant-ending for 52, together 59.0% of name outcomes. There are 18 identical four-hint profiles covering 42 countries. Nauru, Palau, Samoa, Tonga and Tuvalu share all four choices; Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines share another profile. This reduces different-feeling openings even though four alternatives exist per country.
findings.proposedRemedy: Redistribute some repeated name slots among straightforward truthful predicates such as contains O, contains no A, or contains a space, checking the actual-tier breadth of each. Vary a few regional or size choices in repeated full profiles. Avoid first-versus-last comparisons, repeated-letter puzzles and slogans. Unique profiles for every country are unnecessary; prioritize the largest clusters.
findings.confidence: high for concentration; moderate for replay fatigue

findings.problem: Ten Hard-only countries use both no-land-neighbours and island-country alternatives. The verified global catalog sets overlap on 34 of the 35 no-neighbour members; their Jaccard overlap is 0.723. These are not mathematically identical and incomplete geography membership limits exact overlap claims, but both often suggest the same island-search strategy. For these targets, half the rounds can therefore deliver similar geography experiences.
findings.proposedRemedy: Replace one member of selected near-redundant pairs with a different sourced dimension where useful. For the Caribbean targets, a Caribbean location clue has 13 catalog members on Hard; for Malta, a sourced Mediterranean or Europe clue offers a different orientation. Check display support when spreading these replacements so new singleton signatures are not created.
findings.confidence: high for catalog overlap and assignments; moderate for perceived redundancy

findings.problem: The user’s sharper example, all land neighbours smaller by land area, exists in the catalog but is assigned to zero targets and never appears in gameplay. Its verified counts are 4/6/8 and declared possibility unions 15/25/33, so it passes the existing gate in all tiers. Comparisons survive mainly as has-at-least-one-smaller (16 assignments), both-smaller-and-larger (37), and all-larger (20). The four-choice selection omits one of its more distinctive facts.
findings.proposedRemedy: Consider a few independently sourced all-smaller assignments, for example among Brazil, Russia, South Africa or Sweden, while reviewing their reveal strength and other geography choice. It need not be selected everywhere or substituted for every broad neighbour clue. Its small verified set is a review consideration, not a reason to pretend its declared possibility union is exhaustive.
findings.confidence: high for omission and catalog eligibility; moderate for the best target-by-target editorial swap

findings.problem: Selected exact name clues above half of Hard’s pool are first-letter-A–M (117/195) and no-E (109/195), covering 16/780 slots. They can feel weak because they provide no geographic orientation. This is a small exposure, and the simple spelling predicates suit the requested basic style. More broadly, name/numeric/geography remain 25/25/50 percent, but population accounts for 19.6% of all Hard rounds and area only 5.4%. Pure location clues account for 4.36% of Hard rounds; only five of the 170 geography slots for native Hard countries are location clues.
findings.proposedRemedy: Use a review flag, not an automatic rejection, for easy-to-evaluate spelling clues matching more than half of the actual tier. Keep broad numeric bins rather than demanding obscure precise facts. Redistribute a few population slots to existing land-area bands and a few generic border/comparison slots to sourced geographic location where that improves orientation. A maximumFraction change from 70% to 60% would alter no current playable choice by itself, so it is not a useful standalone fix.
findings.confidence: high for counts and category imbalance; moderate for preferred editorial mix

thresholdAndSelectionRecommendations.recommendation: Keep the 4-match/70-percent rule as a baseline integrity heuristic, not an overall fairness verdict.

thresholdAndSelectionRecommendations.reason: Only one is shown. Some broad-name versus small-geography differences are intentional, but a country with two very small familiar geography alternatives warrants attention.

thresholdAndSelectionRecommendations.recommendation: Make diversity an editorial selection objective after correctness and sensible breadth.
thresholdAndSelectionRecommendations.reason: A catalog of 86 phrases yields only 52 playable phrases, highly concentrated name choices, duplicated profiles, and an unused all-smaller fact.

thresholdAndSelectionRecommendations.reason: Small complete groups can be appropriate on Easy, unknown geography lists are not complete truth sets, and numerical familiarity varies among players.

strengths: All 195 targets have four different text alternatives, with one basic name clue, one numeric clue and two geography clues. No selected country repeats exactly the same hint ID.
The game filters alternatives for the actual cumulative tier, shows one stable hint per round, and all current targets retain all four options in every tier where they can be answers.
Independent general-predicate membership, counts, gates, export versions and runtime assignments agree with the bank.

Typical nominal candidate counts rise sensibly from a median 12 on Easy to 29 on Medium and 47 on Hard. Native Hard-country alternatives have at least 12 verified/catalog candidates; unused four-member geography catalog groups do not appear in Hard gameplay.

No selected spelling clue uses the rejected first-versus-last alphabetical comparison or repeated-letter puzzle. Basic spelling, population bands, coasts and land borders are suitable subject matter for the requested style.
Specific coasts, subregions and neighbour relationships retain factual variety; the concern is which facts are assigned and how often, rather than lack of a usable catalog.
limits: This is a source-data and runtime selection review, not a human playtest or an independently sourced accuracy review of every geographical fact.
Geography verified-match sets can be conservative. Declared possible-extra unions are audited as stored bounds but are not independently certified exhaustive truth sets.
Candidate breadth does not measure country familiarity, recognition speed, search habits, map knowledge or enjoyment. Familiar-country and redundancy judgments are editorial assessments.
Expected full-pool frequencies differ slightly from specific journeys because earlier targets are excluded; the report separately reproduces one material exclusion edge case.

Display-support predictability assumes repeated exposure or knowledge of assignments. It must not be represented as a first-time player being able to infer singleton targets from ordinary geography alone.
No proposed changes were implemented. Future new facts or memberships need source review; changing the bank would also require a new content hash and ordinary export verification.
